def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (steps - 1)
    # Allocate output: lat, lon, time
    points = np.full((n_runs, steps, 3), np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
    points[:, 0, :2] = start
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0

    # Constants
    cell_m = terrain.cell_m
    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon

    # To have median distances ~ 2.86 km after duration_s, step about 50m per dt
    # "Route_travelling": move toward steepest descent southwest direction.
    # We'll compute local bearing for steepest downward slope;
    # since southwest is preferred, we bias the bearing toward 225° (3.92699 rad).
    # For each step, walker will move with Tobler speed toward steepest descent close to SW.

    # Precompute bias bearing in rad
    bias_bearing = 3.926990817  # 225 degrees in radians

    # Start variables
    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0])
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1])
    t = np.zeros(n_runs)

    # Walkers’ ok status True until leaving terrain.inside()
    ok = np.ones(n_runs, dtype=bool)

    for i in range(1, steps):
        # Compute elevation at current points
        elev_c = terrain.elev(lat, lon)

        # Sample points small offsets in lat/lon to estimate gradient:
        # Use cell_m in north and east directions (approx 1 deg lat ~ m_lat meters)
        # offsets of cell_m in metres converted to degrees
        d_lat_deg = cell_m / m_lat
        d_lon_deg = cell_m / m_lon

        # Sample elevations around current points for gradient approx
        # We want partial derivatives dE/dx and dE/dy in metres per metre in local east/north directions.
        # East (lon+d_lon_deg), West (lon - d_lon_deg)
        elev_east = terrain.elev(lat, lon + d_lon_deg)
        elev_west = terrain.elev(lat, lon - d_lon_deg)
        dE_dx = (elev_east - elev_west) / (2 * cell_m)  # m/m horizontal east-west slope

        # North (lat + d_lat_deg), South (lat - d_lat_deg)
        elev_north = terrain.elev(lat + d_lat_deg, lon)
        elev_south = terrain.elev(lat - d_lat_deg, lon)
        dE_dy = (elev_north - elev_south) / (2 * cell_m)  # m/m horizontal north-south slope

        # Gradient vector points uphill: [dE_dx east, dE_dy north]
        # Steepest descent is opposite gradient:
        grad_x = -dE_dx  # east component
        grad_y = -dE_dy  # north component

        # Compute bearing of steepest descent:
        # East=0 rad?, atan2(y, x) = north, east
        # We use atan2(grad_y, grad_x)
        bearings = np.arctan2(grad_y, grad_x)

        # Bias bearings toward southwest (225°),
        # Bias blending factor: modulate from 0.7 to 0.9 by slope steepness (stronger bias on steep slopes).
        slope_deg = terrain.slope_deg(lat, lon)
        bias_strength = np.clip((slope_deg - 5) / 20, 0, 1) * 0.2 + 0.7  # 0.7 to 0.9

        # Blend bearing toward bias_bearing:
        # Compute difference [-pi, pi] to bias_bearing, then add fraction of difference back
        diff = bearings - bias_bearing
        diff = (diff + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi) - np.pi
        bearings = bearings - bias_strength * diff
        bearings = (bearings + 2 * np.pi) % (2 * np.pi)

        # Compute step vertical and horizontal distances for speed:
        # dx, dy in metres
        dx = np.cos(bearings) * cell_m
        dy = np.sin(bearings) * cell_m

        # New lat, lon candidates
        lat_new = lat + dy / m_lat
        lon_new = lon + dx / m_lon

        # Compute elevation difference for Tobler speed
        elev_new = terrain.elev(lat_new, lon_new)
        d_elev_m = elev_new - elev_c
        d_horiz_m = np.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)

        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev_m, d_horiz_m)

        # Distance walked this dt constrained by speed * dt:
        dist_max = speed * dt
        # Use a fraction 0.85 of grid cell to control realistic pacing (to fit dist stats)
        step_dist = np.minimum(dist_max, cell_m * 0.85)

        # Normalize bearing vector
        b_x = np.cos(bearings)
        b_y = np.sin(bearings)

        # Update position by step_dist along bearing
        lat_step = lat + (b_y * step_dist) / m_lat
        lon_step = lon + (b_x * step_dist) / m_lon

        # Clamp points inside terrain box
        lat_step, lon_step = terrain.clamp(lat_step, lon_step)

        # Update time
        t_step = t + dt

        # Check inside box:
        inside = terrain.inside(lat_step, lon_step)

        # For walkers outside box, fix them at last position and stop moving
        lat = np.where(inside, lat_step, lat)
        lon = np.where(inside, lon_step, lon)
        t = t_step
        ok = ok & inside

        # Store points
        points[:, i, 0] = lat
        points[:, i, 1] = lon
        points[:, i, 2] = t

    return points, ok

hypothesis.description: Descended southwest off the ridge toward lower elevations via the steepest slope.
hypothesis.rationale: Steepest local descent is southwest and may entice a hiker heading for new scenery.
